name: Zeto transfer
tagline: Zero-knowledge token — anonymous transfer with no notary
concept: Zeto (ZKP): nobody — not even a notary or the regulator — can see amounts or parties. The base ledger holds only proofs and nullifiers, until an owner shares a viewing key.

steps.title: Central Bank mints Zeto cash to Bank A
steps.plain: A wholesale CBDC is issued as a Zeto token. The amount is hidden inside a cryptographic commitment — only Bank A can decrypt its own balance.
steps.tech: Zeto.mint({ to:BankA, amount:1000 }) → commitment 0x… on base ledger

steps.title: Bank A holds anonymous UTXOs
steps.plain: Bank A owns the value as zero-knowledge UTXOs. There is no notary in the loop — no third party sees the balance at all.
steps.tech: UTXO set owned by BankA · spendable with ZK proof of ownership

steps.title: Bank A sends 50 to Bank B (anonymous)
steps.plain: Bank A initiates a private transfer of 50 to Bank B. The amounts and parties never appear in the clear.
steps.tech: Zeto.transfer(): nullify input UTXO → outputs to BankB + change to BankA

steps.title: A zero-knowledge proof is generated
steps.plain: A ZK proof shows the transfer is valid — inputs equal outputs, ownership is correct — without revealing a single number.
steps.tech: snark proof ✓ · proves balance conservation & authorisation

steps.title: Base ledger records nullifier + commitments
steps.plain: The shared ledger stores only a nullifier (so the old note can’t be respent) and new commitments. Anyone can verify it; no one can read it.

steps.title: Bank B receives 50
steps.plain: Bank B can now decrypt its new note: 50. Only Bank B sees this — the Central Bank, the regulator and the public still see nothing.

steps.title: Regulator requests selective disclosure
steps.plain: For an audit, Bank A (or B) shares a viewing key for this one transfer. Now — and only now — the regulator can see A → B · 50. Privacy is selective, not absolute.
